article.title: Political Extinction of Biblical Proportions: Democrats, Never Forgive and Forget!
article.author: Desi Cortez
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. America may be approaching a political extinction of damn-near biblical proportions. Not the extinction of a people, but of a toxic political philosophy that confuses meanness with genius, force and harassment with courage, greed with gumption, and the U.S. Constitution with bathroom tissue. After the November 3 midterms handed Democrats control of Congress, I hear Washington preparing its favorite lullaby: Kumbaya, my Lord, kumbaya. Let’s heal. Let’s move on. Let’s work together. Hold the hell on! Before we serve a war plate of reconciliation with potato salad, somebody ought to explain why victims must forgive while the architects of society-wide suffering collect pensions, television contracts, and speaking fees. Please, kiss me while you screw me, at least, baby. We’re forever told America is eternally divided: Black against White, Christian against Muslim, gay against straight, men against women. Tall against short, you name it. Certainly, those fault lines exist. But beneath them runs the mother of all divisions: TOP TO BOTTOM—the Have-Everythings against the Have-Just-Enoughs against the Have-Not-a-Damn-Things. The champagne-sipping, tax-dodging aristocracy against the people who build their mansions, teach their kids, keep the streets safe, put out fires, heal the sick, cook their meals, and clean their toilets. Related: Should Billionaires Even Exist? The grand American hustle is persuading a struggling White mechanic that his sworn enemy is a struggling Black teacher, or convincing an underpaid Christian waitress that an underpaid Muslim nurse threatens civilization as we know it. Meanwhile, a billionaire who couldn’t distinguish a crescent wrench from a Pillsbury croissant roll purchases another yacht and calls it personal sacrifice. Divide the peasants. Distract the serfs. Then charge them admission to the plantation. And the geography of this hustle is practically color-coded. Study America’s political maps. Blue metropolitan islands float in enormous Republican-red oceans. Atlanta, Houston, Nashville, Denver: cities that often vote differently from the territory surrounding them. Drive fifteen or twenty minutes beyond some diverse urban neighborhoods, and the politics can change faster than Colorado weather. Diversity becomes an invasion. Affordable housing becomes a neighborhood emergency. Equality becomes socialism with suspiciously good manners. Of course, suburbs aren't uniformly Republican, and plenty of Democrats have expensive gates around their expensive homes. That’s precisely my point. A liberal billionaire and a conservative billionaire share more economic interests than either shares with the cashier who bags their groceries. Wealth crosses party lines far more comfortably than working people cross the divisions wealthy interests encourage. Consider the efficiency of this arrangement. When wages stagnate, the poor are told to blame immigrants. When rent rises, they’re instructed to blame the homeless. When schools struggle, they’re encouraged to suspect teachers. The landlord, executive, and political donor stand offstage, counting receipts and congratulating themselves on maintaining order. Which is why Democrats must confront not merely the cruelty, but the economic machinery that makes it profitable. Yet already I hear consultants preaching selective memory: Forget investigations. Focus on grocery prices, gasoline, medicine, housing, jobs. YES! LOWER THE DAMN PRICES! But since when did Congress lose the ability to walk and chew gum? Must Americans choose between affordable insulin and accountability for abuses of power? Apparently, Washington's new strategy is to let suspected wrongdoing slide because eggs cost too much. Start with Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency, that chainsaw carnival where public servants became disposable office furniture. Federal personnel data show the workforce shrank by roughly 264,000 employees between January 2025 and August 2026. Not every departure was a firing, but the damage from rapid reductions deserves examination. Those numbers represent mortgages, medical coverage, college tuition, retirement plans, and families whose financial security was tossed into a billionaire’s spreadsheet. An agency isn’t merely an expense column. It is people and expertise that keep government functioning. A chainsaw can demolish a desk; it cannot answer the telephone after experienced staff disappears. Behind every announcement about “efficiency” sits a family wondering why years of service suddenly count for nothing. You cannot measure public value merely by adding salaries and subtracting benefits. Government isn’t a luxury boutique. It’s supposed to serve the taxpayers the cutters claim to defend. And from livelihoods destroyed, consider families torn apart. Immigration raids, detention, deportation, people terrified by officials acting in the name of enforcement. Remember Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongfully deported to El Salvador despite a court order? A federal judge later dismissed criminal charges against him as vindictive prosecution. That cannot be waved away with a bipartisan handshake. An officer’s badge is not a license to violate rights, and a president’s order does not outrank the Constitution. Where investigations establish illegal detention, excessive force, falsified evidence, or other criminal misconduct, prosecute it. Follow the chain of command. The man ordering wrongdoing from an upholstered chair should not escape scrutiny because somebody else wore the handcuffs. And spare me the argument that accountability is revenge. Every accused person deserves due process, even officials I believe behaved disgracefully. I want evidence, sworn testimony, independent investigations, lawful prosecutions where warranted, and restitution where possible. Not political vendettas. Justice with receipts. We’ve seen what happens when Washington chooses amnesia. In 1974, Gerald Ford pardoned Richard “Tricky Dick” Nixon before a federal criminal trial could test his responsibility for Watergate. Ford called it healing. I call it a lesson the powerful learned all too well: make the scandal big enough, and somebody eventually demands that the country stop discussing it. Related: Castles, Billionaires, and the Cost of Deference Go back further. The Confederacy was defeated on battlefields, but retreat from Reconstruction allowed former Confederates and white supremacists to rebuild political power. Jim Crow followed. America defeated an army without decisively defeating the ideology behind it. Generations who never voted for surrender paid the price. History should alarm Democrats who mistake courtesy for courage. The problem isn’t politeness; it is surrender disguised as virtue . Democracy can welcome disagreement and protect constitutional rights while insisting officials answer for unlawful conduct. Refusing to investigate isn’t mercy. It’s country-club negligence wearing a pressed suit and a smile. And here come the Democrats, potentially preparing another forgiveness festival, complete with television cameras and cucumber sandwiches. MAGA’s most aggressive operators won’t interpret indulgence as statesmanship. They’ll interpret it as proof that bullying works. Then they’ll regroup, raise money, and find another salesman to convince frightened people their neighbors stole the American Dream. The fear machine is already warming up. Gun purchases climbed before Election Day, and gunmakers’ stocks jumped after the Democratic victory. That doesn’t prove a new wave of panic buying overnight, but it exposes a profitable old reflex: convince White America that a political setback means angry Black and Brown neighbors are coming to settle scores. Another imaginary invasion, another magnificent sales opportunity. Meanwhile, consider who actually has reason to fear political violence: newly elected Georgia Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms, who made history as the first Black woman elected governor; Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who unseated Greg Abbott; and nationally prominent targets such as Kamala Harris and the Obamas. I fear threats against them will intensify. Will Democrats wait for a tragedy before taking political intimidation seriously? There’s a reason the words “Never Again” carry such moral force. Americans of color need that same determination against political terror: never again should the victims be told to forget while the instigators are invited back to the banquet. There’s a line in The Magnificent Seven that comes closer to my feelings than a thousand consultants’ memos. Emma Cullen tells Sam Chisolm: “I seek righteousness, as should we all. But I’ll take revenge.” My version? Righteousness with subpoenas. Revenge through lawful accountability, not vigilantism. A courtroom, not a lynch mob. Convictions only when guilt is proved. Let history remember who ordered misconduct, who profited, who looked away, and who grinned for cameras. Democrats cannot criminalize opposition or punish voters for disagreeing. Nor should they. But they can investigate abuses of public power, expose conflicts, demand records, scrutinize spending, and legislate safeguards. Their new congressional majorities take office in January; Trump remains president. Congress cannot manufacture convictions, but it can refuse to be a decorative branch of government. And while they’re at it, confront the platinum-spoon plantation class: tax privileges, corporate favoritism, political money, and wages that barely cover rent. Working Americans shouldn't finance a government that behaves like a customer-service department for billionaires. Lower prices, improve schools, protect healthcare, rebuild institutions. But stop presenting economic relief as a substitute for justice. Bread on the table does not excuse blood on the floor. Wake up, Democrats! This isn’t a Disney production where the wicked king apologizes, the villains discover therapy, and woodland creatures sing about national unity. This is closer to a Quentin Tarantino film, except the victims have no stunt doubles, and the consequences remain after the credits roll. I don’t want political extinction for millions of fellow Americans. I want the extinction of impunity: the notion that wealth buys immunity, cruelty qualifies as patriotism, and public office grants permission to abuse the public. Feed the hungry. House the homeless. Restore careers. Lower the bills. Then investigate wrongdoing, expose profiteers, and hold lawbreakers accountable. Because justice delayed may be justice denied. But justice deliberately abandoned is an engraved invitation to do it all over again. And America has suffered through quite enough sequels to this particular horror show. Fact-check notes: The Democratic congressional victories and the Bottoms and Hinojosa gubernatorial wins are confirmed.
